name: New Mexico

context: NM 340: Cover crops are used to reduce sheet, rill, and wind erosion.
NM 603: Herbaceous wind barriers cut wind speed and erosion on cropland where wind erosion is a resource concern.
cover_rules: NM 340: Direct-seed (no-till) cover crops into standing crop residue for the best wind erosion control and seedling protection.
NM 340: Seeding rates for dryland are half the rate used under irrigation; rates are doubled for broadcast planting.
NM 340: Where soil moisture is limited, terminate the cover crop early enough to conserve moisture for the crop, and leave residue on the surface.
residue: NM 329: No-till needs a crop interval STIR value no greater than 20.
NM 329: Maintain a minimum of 60 percent residue cover on the soil surface throughout the year.
NM 345: Reduced till needs a crop interval STIR value rating no greater than 80, with no primary inversion tillage such as a moldboard plow.
barriers: NM 589: Trap strips are at least 15 feet wide if stubble stays 1 foot or more tall, and at least 25 feet wide if it stays under 1 foot.
NM 603: Barriers need a minimum expected height of 1.5 feet and porosity of 40 to 50 percent; spacing must not exceed 10 times barrier height.
NM 603: Orient barriers perpendicular to the prevailing wind during the critical wind erosion periods.
windbreak: NM 380: The protected zone downwind of a windbreak is 10 times the maximum design height (H) of the tallest row at age 20.
NM 380: Do not use species that are on Federal or State invasive species or noxious weed lists.
roughening: NM 609: Surface roughening is emergency tillage for soils that can form clods and have high wind erosion potential from lack of surface cover.
NM 609: Ridging is done perpendicular to the direction of damaging wind, beginning on the windward edge of the field.
NM 609: It must give a 25% reduction in the potential erosion rate as figured by the current wind erosion technology.
grazing: NM 528: Plan grazing to keep adequate ground cover from canopy, litter and trampled plant residue to reduce soil transport by wind.
NM 528: Minimize grazing animal impact on areas that have high soil erosion potential.
drought: NM 528: Develop and document contingencies for episodic disturbances such as drought and extreme weather events.
NM 340: Do not plant any cover unless soil moisture is available.
seeding: NM 550: Seed native grasses at 40 seeds per square foot, using a no-till drill into existing cover where possible.
NM 550: Broadcast or frost seeding raises the rate from 40 seeds per square foot to 60-80 seeds per square foot.
NM 550: Place seed 1/2 inch to 1 inch deep unless it is very small, then about 1/4 inch.
dont_seed: NM 550: Do not apply any nitrogen at planting of native warm-season grasses; it only encourages weeds.
disturbed: NM 342: If strong erosive winds are expected, protect the critical area with barriers such as snow fence or wind screens.
dunes: NM 342: Plants for sand dunes must survive being buried by blowing sand, sand blasting, drought and low nutrient supply.
NM 342: Include sand trapping devices such as sand fences or brush matting in dune stabilization plans.

NM 340: Spring oats are seeded 3/1 to 5/15 in most zones.
NM 340: Forage sorghums and foxtail millet go in 5/1 to 8/1 in HP-1, HP-2, CP-1, CP-2, CP-3, WP and ND.
